annotations.description: On Turn 1 with only Polluted Delta on the battlefield and the opponent having just played an Undercity Sewers (tapped), there's no reason not to crack Polluted Delta during the opponent's end step or during combat to get a land untapped. By not activating Polluted Delta at all during Turn 1, the player is delaying their mana development. More importantly, cracking the fetch now would enable having 2 mana available on Turn 2 (the fetched land plus whatever land they play). The player will likely need to crack it on their own turn 2 anyway, but doing it at end of opponent's turn or during this combat step is free - it costs nothing extra and keeps options open. However, since they're going to untap and can crack it on their own turn before playing a land, the actual tempo loss is minimal. The reasoning given ('sacrificing it isn't beneficial at this point') is incorrect - you always want to fetch at the last possible moment before you need the mana, but not fetching at all this turn when you could is a slight missed optimization for information hiding and revolt enabling.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Polluted Delta to fetch an Island or Swamp (likely Island to support blue-heavy hand with Consult the Star Charts, Subtlety, Wan Shi Tong), getting ahead on mana development and enabling 2 mana on Turn 2

annotations.description: Fetching Watery Grave off Bloodstained Mire costs 2 life (paying for the shockland untapped) for UB mana when the player already has Undercity Sewers providing UB. The player wants to cast Psychic Frog (UB) or Gran-Gran (U) on turn 2. However, fetching a basic Swamp would provide B mana for free (no shock cost), and combined with Undercity Sewers (which provides U or B), would allow casting Psychic Frog (U from Sewers, B from Swamp) without paying 2 life. At 17 life with Thoughtseize already cast, life is a meaningful resource, especially in a format like Modern. A basic Swamp achieves the same mana flexibility for turn 2 plays without the life cost.

annotations.description: Subtlety was evoked (exiling Wan Shi Tong from hand to pay the evoke cost), which creates two triggered abilities: the ETB to bounce a creature/planeswalker spell, and the evoke sacrifice trigger. By putting the evoke sacrifice trigger on the stack first (resolving last), the ETB would resolve first, letting you target a spell. But by choosing the order that puts the sacrifice trigger on top (resolving first), Subtlety is sacrificed before the ETB can be used meaningfully. However, looking at the board state, the opponent has no creature or planeswalker spells on the stack, so the ETB has no valid targets anyway. The Subtlety was likely evoked to get it into play temporarily or for some other purpose. Since there are no spells to target, the ordering doesn't actually matter here.

annotations.description: Activating Field of Ruin costs 2 mana and sacrifices the land, leaving Llama4 Johnny with only 1 land (the basic Island they'll search for) plus the new basic. This is a terrible time to use it - the opponent's lands are already tapped, so destroying one doesn't prevent them from doing anything this turn. Meanwhile, Llama4 Johnny has Sheoldred's Edict and Fatal Push in hand to deal with Psychic Frog, which is the actual threat. Using Field of Ruin here wastes the turn's mana on destroying a land when they should be answering the creature. Additionally, the opponent has Psychic Frog on board which will generate card advantage if it connects. Fatal Push with revolt (from sacrificing Field of Ruin) could kill it, but they could just cast Fatal Push targeting the Frog since it has MV 2, without needing revolt. The Field of Ruin activation also triggers Wan Shi Tong in the graveyard... wait, Wan Shi Tong is in the graveyard not on the battlefield. But importantly, both players search their libraries when Field of Ruin resolves, and the opponent gets a free basic land - so you're trading your Field of Ruin to replace one of their nonbasics with a basic, a marginal exchange at best, especially when you need mana to cast your spells. They should cast Consult the Star Charts (costs 1U with 2 lands) to find more resources, or hold up Fatal Push/Sheoldred's Edict to answer the Psychic Frog.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Field of Ruin to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land when the opponent's lands were already tapped and a Psychic Frog threatened to generate card advantage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Consult the Star Charts for 1U to look at top 2 cards and find a land drop or answer, or simply pass to hold up Fatal Push and Sheoldred's Edict to deal with Psychic Frog on the opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Casting Gran-Gran on Turn 4 precombat main is suboptimal for several reasons. First, the opponent has 2 open lands (one untapped Island) which could represent interaction. More importantly, Haiku ESPN should be attacking with Psychic Frog first before casting creatures - if Frog connects, they draw a card which gives more information. Additionally, Gran-Gran's tap trigger (draw/discard on becoming tapped) means it won't do anything this turn since it has summoning sickness. Casting it post-combat or holding up Spell Pierce mana would be better. With the opponent at only 2 lands and one tapped, this is a window to press the Psychic Frog advantage while keeping up Spell Pierce for protection.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Gran-Gran ({U}) precombat, tapping out of blue mana and unable to hold up Spell Pierce
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Psychic Frog first (potentially drawing a card on hit), then decide whether to cast Gran-Gran or hold up Spell Pierce depending on what's drawn and the opponent's response. Alternatively, just pass with Spell Pierce up since Frog is already applying pressure.

annotations.description: Attacking with Gran-Gran is risky and suboptimal. Gran-Gran is a 1/2 that draws a card when it becomes tapped - but attacking with it into an empty board only deals 1 damage while exposing it to potential blockers or removal during combat. More importantly, Gran-Gran's tap trigger for card draw/discard could be leveraged more carefully. The opponent has no blockers so there's no immediate risk, but the real issue is that attacking with Gran-Gran means tapping it, which triggers its draw/discard ability. While the draw is nice, being forced to discard when you have a hand of Fatal Push, Fatal Push, Spell Pierce, Persist, and Archon of Cruelty means discarding one of these valuable cards. Discarding Archon of Cruelty to set up Persist is actually a reasonable line, so this could work out well. However, the player's reasoning shows no strategic thought about what to discard - they just said 'LET'S GO TO THE RACES!' which suggests they didn't consider whether this was optimal. Attacking with just Psychic Frog (which draws a card on combat damage and can be pumped with discards) while keeping Gran-Gran back to use more deliberately could have been better.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Psychic Frog and Gran-Gran
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Psychic Frog. Psychic Frog draws on combat damage and can be pumped by discarding. Gran-Gran's tapped trigger forces a discard that should be timed more deliberately. That said, if the plan was to discard Archon to set up Persist, attacking Gran-Gran is defensible.

annotations.description: Missed the opportunity to discard Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog's ability, which would both grow the Frog and set up a devastating Persist reanimation of Archon next turn (as a 5/5 flyer with its powerful ETB trigger). With only 2 lands and Persist in hand, this is the primary game plan for this deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Psychic Frog's discard ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Psychic Frog by discarding Archon of Cruelty to put a +1/+1 counter on it, then cast Persist next turn targeting Archon of Cruelty in the graveyard to reanimate it as a 5/5 flyer

annotations.description: Llama4 Johnny activated Field of Ruin (costing 2 mana + sacrificing the land) to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land, but this leaves them with essentially no mana on board (just an Island after searching for a basic). More importantly, Field of Ruin lets each player search their library for a basic land - the opponent has Gran-Gran on the battlefield, and searching doesn't trigger it (Gran-Gran triggers on tap, not on opponent searching). However, the real issue is that using Field of Ruin here costs the player their second land and 2 mana, leaving them unable to cast any of their interaction (Counterspell, Sheoldred's Edict, Fatal Push, Force of Negation with mana) on the opponent's turn. The opponent has Psychic Frog (a serious threat that grows) and Gran-Gran on board, and Llama4 has excellent reactive cards in hand that all require mana. Destroying a land while leaving yourself unable to interact is a poor trade. They should have held up Counterspell or other interaction, or cast Consult the Star Charts to find a land drop and develop their mana base instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Field of Ruin to destroy an opponent's nonbasic land, sacrificing their own land and spending 2 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Consult the Star Charts (costs 1U with the two available lands) to dig for a third land and develop mana, or simply pass to hold up Counterspell/Fatal Push for the opponent's turn

annotations.description: Playing Undercity Sewers (which enters tapped) instead of Watery Grave means the player loses access to one mana this turn. With Psychic Frog on board wanting to attack, and holding Spell Pierce and two Fatal Pushes, having maximum mana available is important for interaction. Watery Grave would enter untapped (paying 2 life) and provide immediate mana, while Undercity Sewers enters tapped and wastes the turn's mana potential. The opponent only has 2 lands (one tapped), so this turn is a window to be aggressive with Psychic Frog while holding up interaction.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) as the land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Watery Grave (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) to have 4 mana available, enabling better interaction options like holding up Spell Pierce plus Fatal Push, or having more flexibility during combat.

annotations.description: Haiku ESPN has Psychic Frog with no opposing blockers, Archon of Cruelty in hand (uncastable at 3 lands), and Persist in hand. Discarding Archon to pump Psychic Frog before combat would deal extra damage, draw a card on combat damage (replacing the discard), AND set up a devastating Persist to reanimate Archon of Cruelty for just 2 mana. Instead, they passed with no action, citing 'holding up Fatal Push' despite the opponent having no creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Psychic Frog's discard ability before combat.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog to put a +1/+1 counter on it, then attack with the pumped Frog to draw a card on combat damage, setting up Persist to reanimate Archon of Cruelty on a future turn.

annotations.description: Attacking with Gran-Gran into an opponent with open mana is risky but debatable. Gran-Gran is a 1/2 that provides card filtering and future cost reduction. The opponent has Field of Ruin (tapped) and an Island with no cards in hand visible, but Llama4 Johnny could have drawn removal. More importantly, Gran-Gran's tap trigger draws and discards regardless of whether it attacks or not - but Gran-Gran needs to become tapped to trigger, so attacking is the primary way to get that trigger. However, the opponent has Sheoldred's Edict and Fatal Push known from the earlier Thoughtseize reveal. If opponent has Fatal Push, they could kill Gran-Gran in combat (revolt is easy with Field of Ruin). Attacking Psychic Frog alone would be safer - it draws a card on combat damage and can be pumped with discards. That said, Gran-Gran as a 1/2 is not a huge loss and the draw+discard trigger has value, and the opponent only has 2 mana (1 untapped Island), so Fatal Push would require the Island. This is borderline - attacking both is aggressive but Gran-Gran is somewhat expendable and the trigger value is real.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Psychic Frog and Gran-Gran
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Psychic Frog to protect Gran-Gran as a valuable engine piece, especially since opponent could have drawn Fatal Push or other interaction. Gran-Gran's long-term value with cost reduction and card filtering likely outweighs 1 damage.

annotations.description: Failed to discard Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog, missing the core reanimation combo. Archon of Cruelty in the graveyard + Persist in hand = a 5/5 flying Archon as early as next turn, which would likely win the game against an opponent with only lands and no board. Fatal Push has minimal value when the opponent has no creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Fatal Push instead of Archon of Cruelty
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty to Psychic Frog to set up Persist reanimation next turn, creating an overwhelming 5/5 flying threat with a devastating ETB trigger.

annotations.description: Discarded Bloodstained Mire (a useful fetchland that enables revolt for Fatal Push and provides mana fixing) instead of the duplicate Gran-Gran which is completely dead since Gran-Gran is legendary and one is already on the battlefield. Additionally, the ideal discard plan would be to pitch Archon of Cruelty + duplicate Gran-Gran, setting up a devastating turn-5 Persist targeting Archon for just 2 mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Bloodstained Mire and Persist
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty and the duplicate Gran-Gran. This puts Archon in the graveyard for Persist reanimation (2 mana for a 6/6 flying with a powerful ETB) while getting rid of the dead legendary duplicate. Keep both lands for mana development.

annotations.description: Discarding Abhorrent Oculus instead of Archon of Cruelty misses the opportunity to set up the Persist reanimation combo. Archon of Cruelty in the graveyard + Persist (only 2 mana) = a 5/5 flying Archon with a devastating ETB trigger (opponent sacs a creature, discards, loses 3; you draw and gain 3). This is vastly more impactful than trying to cast Abhorrent Oculus which requires 6 graveyard cards to exile.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Abhorrent Oculus
annotations.betterLine: Discard Archon of Cruelty to set up Persist reanimation next turn for a 2-mana 5/5 flyer with game-swinging ETB trigger

annotations.description: Discarded Abhorrent Oculus, which costs only 3 mana (with 6 graveyard exiles) and was their most castable threat with only 3 lands in play. They have two Archon of Cruelty in hand (8 mana each, uncastable for many turns) and a Persist in hand that could reanimate a discarded Archon.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Abhorrent Oculus, losing their only copy of a 3-mana 5/5 flyer that was close to castable.
annotations.betterLine: Discard an Archon of Cruelty instead. This preserves the castable Abhorrent Oculus and sets up a powerful Persist line to reanimate the Archon for just 2 mana next turn.

annotations.description: Orcish Bowmasters is one of the best cards in Llama4 Johnny's hand against this board state. The opponent has Gran-Gran (1/2) which triggers card draw when tapped, and Psychic Frog (1/2) which draws cards on combat damage. Bowmasters punishes extra card draws with damage and amass, and at 2 mana with flash it could be deployed at instant speed to kill Gran-Gran (ping for 1 + amass, then the orc army can block or trade). With only 3 lands in play and needing interaction, Bowmasters is a high-value card that provides both a body and repeated value against a deck that draws extra cards frequently. Meanwhile, the hand has redundant removal (2x Fatal Push, 2x Sheoldred's Edict) and redundant counters (Counterspell, Force of Negation, Spell Snare). Discarding a duplicate removal spell or the second Spell Snare would have been much better.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Orcish Bowmasters
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Spell Snare or one of the duplicate Sheoldred's Edicts. Bowmasters is uniquely powerful here as a flash creature that punishes the opponent's extra card draws from Gran-Gran and Psychic Frog, and can immediately kill Gran-Gran when deployed.

annotations.description: Discarded Island when only having 3 lands on the battlefield and needing land drops to develop. There's a duplicate legendary Gran-Gran in hand that can't be cast without sacrificing the one already on the battlefield, making it a much better discard option. Alternatively, discarding an Archon of Cruelty would fuel the Persist reanimation plan.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Island
annotations.betterLine: Discard the second Gran-Gran (legendary duplicate) or an Archon of Cruelty (to set up Persist reanimation with one already in graveyard)

annotations.description: Discarded Spell Snare which uniquely and efficiently (1 mana) counters Persist (MV 2), a critical threat given the opponent has Archon of Cruelty and 2x Abhorrent Oculus in graveyard with Persist also in graveyard (but may have more copies). Having 3 Fatal Push is clearly redundant when opponent only has 2 small creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spell Snare to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard the third Fatal Push, as it's the most redundant card. Spell Snare efficiently answers Persist and other MV 2 threats for just 1 mana, preserving mana for additional responses.

annotations.description: Discarded Emperor of Bones, a castable and powerful 2-drop that can reanimate creatures from graveyards, instead of the duplicate Gran-Gran which is uncastable because Gran-Gran is legendary and one is already on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Emperor of Bones
annotations.betterLine: Discard the duplicate Gran-Gran, which is a dead card while the current Gran-Gran is on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Discarded Watery Grave instead of a duplicate legendary Gran-Gran. With only 4 lands on board and expensive Archon of Cruelty in hand (8 mana), the extra land drop would help reach higher mana counts. A second Gran-Gran is largely dead due to the legendary rule since one is already on the battlefield.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Watery Grave and Fatal Push
annotations.betterLine: Discard duplicate Gran-Gran and Fatal Push (or second Fatal Push), keeping the land to help eventually cast Archon of Cruelty or have more mana flexibility

annotations.description: With only 3 lands (Island, Field of Ruin, Steam Vents) and 8 cards in hand including reactive spells like Counterspell, Force of Negation, and removal, Llama4 Johnny should prioritize using Field of Ruin to destroy one of the opponent's nonbasic lands. This would get them a basic land (fixing mana and ramping to 4 lands), thin their deck, and disrupt the opponent's mana. Casting Consult the Star Charts with only 3 lands means looking at only 3 cards and putting 1 in hand - a mediocre outcome. Additionally, they're stuck on 3 lands and need to develop their mana to cast their spells. Field of Ruin costs 2+T+sacrifice, which they could activate, getting a basic land untapped. This would help them hold up Counterspell or double Fatal Push next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Consult the Star Charts (looking at only 3 cards, keeping 1) using 2 mana, leaving only Field of Ruin untapped.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Field of Ruin targeting one of the opponent's nonbasic lands (Watery Grave or Undercity Sewers) to search for a basic land, increasing land count to 3 untapped lands and disrupting opponent's mana. This also enables holding up Counterspell on the opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Llama4 Johnny is at 9 life facing attackers and has only 3 lands on the battlefield (Island, Field of Ruin, Steam Vents). Their hand is loaded with reactive spells (3x Fatal Push, 2x Sheoldred's Edict, Counterspell, Force of Negation) but critically needs more mana to cast multiple spells per turn. However, looking at the choices - Flooded Strand, Swamp, Sheoldred's Edict - the player already has 3 Fatal Pushes and 2 Sheoldred's Edicts in hand, so another Edict is less needed than a land drop. Flooded Strand is a fetchland that can find Islands or Swamps, which is flexible. But Swamp would be the better pick here since it enters untapped immediately (Flooded Strand costs 1 life to crack when at 9 life, and the player already has blue sources). With the board state showing they need to deploy removal efficiently, getting a Swamp that enters untapped for free is slightly better than a fetchland that costs a life point and requires an additional step. The life total of 9 makes that 1 life relevant against the attacking creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Flooded Strand over Swamp from Consult the Star Charts
annotations.betterLine: Choose Swamp - it enters untapped without costing life, providing the black mana needed for Fatal Push and Sheoldred's Edict while preserving the precious life total at 9 life.

annotations.description: Llama4 Johnny fetched a basic Island when their hand contains 5 black spells (3x Fatal Push, 2x Sheoldred's Edict) and they have ZERO black mana sources on the battlefield. At 8 life with the opponent attacking for 2+ per turn, they desperately need to start removing threats. Fetching Island leaves them completely unable to cast any of their removal spells.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched a basic Island, leaving them with no black mana sources despite a hand full of black removal spells.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Watery Grave (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) to gain access to black mana, enabling Fatal Push on Psychic Frog or Gran-Gran this turn. Even going to 6 life is worth it to start interacting with the opponent's board.

annotations.description: Discarded Thoughtseize instead of the redundant second Gran-Gran. With Gran-Gran already on the battlefield (legendary), the second copy is dead weight until the first dies. Thoughtseize could strip a counterspell or removal from the opponent's hand at 6 life, potentially enabling lethal attacks.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Persist and Thoughtseize
annotations.betterLine: Discard Persist and one of the two Gran-Gran copies, keeping Thoughtseize to strip the opponent's answers when they're at 6 life.

annotations.description: Llama4 Johnny fetched Island with Field of Ruin while having ZERO black mana sources on board and a hand full of black spells (3x Fatal Push, 2x Sheoldred's Edict). After this fetch, they have Islands and Steam Vents but cannot cast any of their 5 black removal spells, leaving them unable to interact with the opponent's creatures at 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched a basic Island, leaving them with no black mana sources.
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Watery Grave (paying 2 life to enter untapped, going to 3 life) to gain access to black mana, enabling Fatal Push and Sheoldred's Edict to deal with Psychic Frog and Gran-Gran. Even at 3 life, being able to remove threats is more important than preserving 2 life with no way to interact.

annotations.description: Discarding Orcish Bowmasters when facing repeated card draw from Gran-Gran and Psychic Frog seems questionable. Bowmasters is excellent against the opponent's strategy since Gran-Gran draws a card when tapped (triggering Bowmasters) and Psychic Frog draws on combat damage. With 5 lands in play, casting Bowmasters is easy, and it provides both a body to block and punishment for the opponent's card draw engine. One of the three Fatal Pushes or one of the two Sheoldred's Edicts would be more redundant to discard.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Orcish Bowmasters
annotations.betterLine: Discard a third Fatal Push or second Sheoldred's Edict, keeping Orcish Bowmasters as a powerful answer to the opponent's card-draw-heavy gameplan with Gran-Gran and Psychic Frog.

annotations.description: Discarded Spell Pierce over a duplicate legendary Gran-Gran. There's already a Gran-Gran on the battlefield, making extra copies completely uncastable due to the legend rule. Spell Pierce, while somewhat weakened against an opponent with 5 mana, still has potential utility as a cheap counterspell to protect Psychic Frog from removal. Both could serve as Psychic Frog discard fodder, but Spell Pierce has strictly more utility than a dead legendary duplicate.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spell Pierce
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the duplicate Gran-Grans, which cannot be cast due to the legend rule with Gran-Gran already on the battlefield.

annotations.description: Discarded Abhorrent Oculus, which is actually castable at 3 mana (2U + exile 6 from graveyard, which they have 19 cards to work with) and provides a powerful 5/5 flyer with manifest dread value. annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the three Archon of Cruelty copies. They already have Archon in the graveyard for Persist, and Abhorrent Oculus is actually castable with current mana and provides immediate board impact.

annotations.description: Playing Field of Ruin instead of Polluted Delta is suboptimal. Polluted Delta is a fetch land that can find an Island or Swamp, giving mana flexibility and thinning the deck. Field of Ruin requires spending 2 mana plus sacrificing itself to destroy a nonbasic land, which is a tempo-negative play. The opponent has Undercity Sewers and Watery Grave as nonbasic lands, but spending 2 mana to destroy one when you're at 5 life facing creatures on board is not a priority. Playing Polluted Delta first gives you access to 5 mana (4 Islands + Steam Vents) plus the Delta ready to fetch if needed, and you can always play Field of Ruin next turn. Additionally, the reasoning says 'Let's play Flooded Strand' which doesn't match either choice, suggesting confused decision-making.

annotations.betterLine: Play Polluted Delta as the land for turn, keeping it available to fetch at instant speed for revolt (enabling Fatal Push to kill 4-mana-value creatures) or to fix mana. Field of Ruin could be played on a later turn.

annotations.betterLine: Fetch Swamp (enters untapped, no life cost) to gain access to black mana and be able to cast Fatal Push or Sheoldred's Edict to deal with the opponent's threats. Even Watery Grave at 2 life would be better than having no black sources at all.
